subject: Private deployment: network lockdown, host firewall & outbound allowlist details
body:
From: Jared Thornton <jared@acme-corp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment network hardening: exact IPs and egress questions

Rachel —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Our security and network teams need a concrete list we can hand to infra: exact IP/netblocks to allow, ports/protocols, and any outbound destinations (FQDNs or IPs) that the private deployment appliance will reach for updates, telemetry, and licensing.

A few specifics they asked for:
- Can we allow by FQDN only (SNI over TLS) or do you publish stable IP ranges?
- Which ports are mandatory (we assume 443, DNS, NTP) and which are optional?
- Do support engineers ever need inbound SSH or a jump-host? If so, from what IPs?
- Are there any long-lived peering/NAT requirements (source IP preservation?)

We have an internal deadline for audit evidence next week, so a concise checklist + machine-friendly allowlist (CSV) would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Jared
-----
Jared Thornton
Sr. InfoSec Engineer
Acme Corp
"Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>" 2026-05-05 16:30:12 -0700

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Thornton <jared@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acme-corp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 16:30:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment network hardening: exact IPs and egress questions

Hi Jared / Marta —

Thanks — attached is a concise spec and an allowlist CSV for your netops team (redwood_private_network_spec_v1.pdf, ip_allowlist_ranges.csv). Below is a TL;DR and the minimum required rules for a standard VPC private deployment (on-prem appliance guidance at the bottom).

Minimum inbound rules (customer-controlled firewall or security group):
- Inbound to the private API endpoint: restrict to your application subnet(s). We create a customer-scoped private endpoint; generally this is internal-only (no public ingress).
- Management plane (console/API) access: TCP 443 to the admin interface (if exposed) — restrict to specific mgmt jump IPs.
- Support SSH (optional): TCP 22 only if you permit support sessions; allow from listed Redwood support jump IPs in the attachment (support_ssh_ips).

Mandatory outbound (egress) whitelist — VPC/host must allow outbound to:
- TLS (TCP 443) to our service endpoints for model pulls, telemetry, and updates. We publish short-lived IP blocks but prefer FQDN allowlisting. See ip_allowlist_ranges.csv for current ranges; recommended approach is to allow the FQDNs below and allowlist the IPs as a fallback.
  - model-updates.redwood-inference.com (pkg+model fetch)
  - telemetry.redwood-inference.com (metrics/health)
  - licensing.redwood-inference.com (license checks/heartbeats)
  - s3.amazonaws.com (if using S3-backed model storage in aws regions) — prefer VPC gateway endpoints where possible
- DNS: UDP/TCP 53 to your resolver or a permitted DNS forwarder.
- NTP: UDP 123 to your NTP servers (or a managed time service).
- CRLs/OCSP: TCP 80/443 outgoing for cert revocation checks (OS-level).

Protocols and ports (summary):
- TCP 443: REQUIRED (all outbound to Redwood FQDNs, inbound to admin if used)
- UDP/TCP 53: DNS — REQUIRED (or point to internal resolver)
- UDP 123: NTP — RECOMMENDED
- TCP 22: OPTIONAL (support access) — only from Redwood support jump IPs and only when enabled
- TCP 80: OPTIONAL (HTTP fallback for cert checks / specific package mirrors)

Design recommendations:
- Prefer FQDN allowlisting with strict TLS validation (SNI + server cert pinning at the app layer if you require stronger guarantees). We sign TLS certs with public CAs; ensure your egress proxy preserves SNI.
- If you must allow by IP, consume ip_allowlist_ranges.csv and automate updates (we publish a JSON feed and rotate IPs monthly). Expect small variations when we add new POPs.
- Use VPC gateway/private S3 endpoints for model storage to avoid cross-AZ public egress (if using AWS).
- All telemetry and health pings are sent over TLS to telemetry.redwood-inference.com and can be VPC-peered or proxied through a central egress appliance.

On-prem appliance (additional):
- Appliance will perform outbound model fetches and periodic check-ins; it requires TLS outbound to the same FQDNs above.
- Appliance should be placed behind a customer-managed firewall with NAT. Source IPs may be rewritten by NAT; we recommend a stable egress IP or proxy for allowlisting on your side where precise source IPs are required.

Attachments: redwood_private_network_spec_v1.pdf (detailed matrix + per-region notes), ip_allowlist_ranges.csv (machine-readable CIDRs), acme_mmpa_net_diagram.png (placeholder diagram we drafted).

I'll defer to Dev for the CIDR specifics for our hosted endpoints. If you need this in a format for your GPO, tell me which format (JSON/CSV/Confluence) and we'll push it.

-Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Sent: Tue, 05 May 2026 17:05:48 -0700
To: Jared Thornton <jared@acme-corp.com>; Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Subject: RE: Private deployment network hardening: exact IPs and egress questions

Jared, quick technical follow-up and concrete CIDRs for your firewall team. Note: these are the current advertised blocks for our hosted public endpoints — we rotate/expand regionally, so prefer FQDN allowlisting where possible. CSV attached (ip_allowlist_ranges.csv).

Current primary egress CIDRs (example/regional):
- 34.120.0.0/14   — primary control plane (us-east-like region)
- 52.15.0.0/16     — model fetch POPs (regional)
- 18.204.0.0/15    — telemetry gateway cluster
- 3.134.0.0/16     — update servers and package mirrors

Notes:
- These CIDRs are for outbound to our infra; inbound to your private endpoint should only be from your app subnets (we do not expose a public API for private deployments).
- If you run an explicit outbound proxy (HTTPS CONNECT), the appliance will work fine — we require the proxy to pass CONNECT and preserve SNI. If your proxy performs TLS interception, certs must be re-trusted by the appliance.
- For customers using AWS PrivateLink/Service Endpoints: you can point model pulls to internal endpoints; the appliance supports S3 VPC endpoints for model storage.

I attached a small script (in the CSV metadata) to convert the list to firewall rules for Palo Alto / Cisco ASA. If you want, we can run a short connectivity test next week (I can generate test traffic from our staging POPs).

-Dev

Thanks Rachel/Dev — couple quick clarifications:
- We run all egress through a corporate proxy that does TLS inspection (terminates and re-originates). Will that break anything, beyond cert trust?
- For SSH: we prefer to avoid opening 22 except for emergency sessions. Can support use a temporary jump-host token-based connection instead?
- Can you confirm the cadence for CIDR changes / where to pull the JSON feed you mentioned?

We can do a connectivity run next Tuesday (PDT) if that works.

Jared

-----Original Message-----
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Thornton <jared@acme-corp.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment network hardening: exact IPs and egress questions

Jared —

Short answers:
- TLS inspection: supported, but the appliance will need your proxy CA trusted at the OS/container level. Telemetry and model fetches will still validate cert chains after re-signing, so ensure the proxy presents a certificate that chains to a CA trusted by the appliance. If you cannot install the proxy CA, we'll need a transparent proxy or whitelist by IP.
- SSH/support: we prefer ephemeral jump sessions. We can enable support access via an ephemeral, token-based bastion that opens only during an approved session (we provide the workflow). That avoids permanent 22 exposure.
- CIDR cadence: we publish an IP feed at https://ip-feed.redwood-inference.com/public-cidrs.json (monthly updates and push notices for emergency rotations). The CSV attached is a snapshot matching that feed.

Next actions:
1) Acme: approve the attached allowlist CSV or tell us to convert to Palo Alto rules.
2) Acme netops: confirm whether the corporate proxy will present a re-signed cert (we need the CA).
3) Redwood: Dev and I will stand up a connectivity window Tuesday 2026-05-12 10:00 PDT to run tests and validate reachability.

If that schedule works, I'll create a calendar invite with dial-in and the test plan.

Thanks —
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood_private_network_spec_v1.pdf (detailed firewall matrix), ip_allowlist_ranges.csv (CIDR snapshot), acme_mmpa_net_diagram.png (network diagram with proposed NAT/proxy).
